title: How the Printing Press Changed the World
paragraphs: Before the printing press, every book was copied by hand. A writer needed many months to finish one book, so books were rare and very expensive. Only rich people and churches had them.
Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg, a craftsman in the German city of Mainz, built a printing press. He used small metal letters that he could move and use again.
Workers put the letters together to make a page. Then they added ink and pressed paper on it. They could print hundreds of the same page in a short time.
Soon there were printing presses in many European cities. Books became cheaper, and more people learned to read. News and new ideas travelled faster than ever before.
